title: Criminology, B.S. (College of the Liberal Arts)
notes: Pre-First-Year/Second-Year-Seminar curriculum, built from the archived 2022-23 bulletin's own Program Requirements and Suggested Academic Plan tabs (fetched directly this pass, raw HTML cross-checked against the page's own printed semester subtotals and 'Total Credits 121', per the known WebFetch-summary confabulation risk on archive.psu.edu pages). Confirmed structurally identical through 2023-24 and 2024-25 (see CRIMBS-2023.json / CRIMBS-2024.json's own notes) -- the 121-credit, no-LA-83/no-LA-283 curriculum was replaced starting with the 2025-26 edition (see CRIMBS-2025.json / CRIMBS-2026.json), which added LA 83 (First-Year Seminar, 1.5 cr) and LA 283 (Second-Year Seminar, 1.5 cr) and raised the total to 124 credits -- the same 121-to-124 curriculum change found for the sibling B.A. (see CRIM-2022.json through CRIM-2026.json). This year's archive page's Common Requirements for the Major (CRIM/CRIMJ/SOC 12, CRIM/CRIMJ 100, CRIM 249, CRIM 250W, STAT 200), its four named Options (Business/Public Administration, Computing and Statistics, Legal Studies, Social Science Research), and the Computing and Statistics option's own course list (SOC 470, STAT 480, and a 16cr list of CAS 483/CMPSC 203/MATH 110+111 or 140+141/MIS 204/STAT 460/462/464) this plan models are otherwise identical to CRIMBS-2026.json's own current-year requirements -- only the two seminars and the resulting credit total differ. Built by taking CRIMBS-2026.json's own already-fixed base and removing the LA 83 item from Semester 1 (target_credits reduced 13.5 -> 12) and the 'Second-Year Liberal Arts Seminar' slot from Semester 4 (target_credits reduced 16.5 -> 15), with 'LA' dropped from departments since no LA course appears anywhere else in this plan -- mirroring the identical LA-department-only-since-2025 convention already established in CRIM-2022.json for the sibling B.A. Real gap this year's archive shares with 2026's: STAT 200's real prereq_groups require MATH 21, which needs MATH 4, which needs MATH 3 -- none of these appear anywhere in the bulletin's own suggested plan for any year checked (2022-23 through the live 2026-27 edition), so (mirroring CRIMBS-2026.json's own fix for the identical gap) MATH 3 -> MATH 4 -> MATH 21 are kept explicit across Semesters 1-3. The option's own prescribed SOC 470 needs SOC 207 (not otherwise scheduled anywhere in this plan) -- kept explicit in Semester 4, and the common 'SOC 1/3/5' requirement stays narrowed to literal SOC 1 so the SOC 1 -> SOC 207 -> SOC 470 chain resolves deterministically, same as CRIMBS-2026.json. The department's own real, current 'CRIM_BS-Computing-and-Statistics-Checksheet.pdf' requirement of MATH 110+111 or MATH 140+141 as a mandatory calculus pair (absent from the bulletin's own generic 16cr 'select from list' wording) is not dated to a specific catalog year and is treated here as stable across years, same as CRIMBS-2026.json's own handbook-verification-pass finding. Race/Ethnicity/Gender and 4XX CRIM Core/Non-Core match patterns are reused verbatim from CRIMBS-2026.json's own department-checksheet-sourced lists: this year's archive page, like every other edition checked, only names these as generic 'from list' categories without publishing the list content on the program page itself, so there is no year-specific bulletin list to verify against -- flagged as an inherited assumption, not independently re-verified for 2022-23, matching CRIM-2022.json's own identical caveat for the sibling B.A. CRIM 249/CRIM 250W's own prereq_groups being empty in the shared crim_catalog.json is a catalog-level (not degree-plan-year-specific) gap already flagged in CRIMBS-2026.json's own notes and left alone here for the same reason: catalogs/*.json is out of scope for a degree-plan-year fix. CAMPUS CHECK: this year's archive page's own 'Where can I complete this program?' section reads 'Begin Campus: Any Penn State Campus' / 'End Campus: University Park' -- identical to the live 2026-27 page -- confirming this B.S. is, and has been, a University-Park-only degree (Commonwealth-campus enrollment is a 2+2 feeder into this same UP curriculum, not a separate program), so no Erie/Brandywine campus addition applies to this major.
